comparison: Perfect agreement on phenotypic claims C9-C15. Both evaluations support the differential roles of CobB and CobQ based on deletion mutant phenotypes. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and appropriate controls, while peer reviewers accept these observations without methodological critique.

Disagreement on MS/MS evidence for deacetylation mechanism (C29-C30). OpenEval finds the LC MS/MS data and synthetic peptide experiments provide strong support, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to missing supplementary data documentation and incomplete data presentation.

Complete agreement on KEGG pathway enrichment analysis (C45). Both evaluations accept this bioinformatics finding as appropriately supporting the functional characterization of AhCobQ substrates, treating it as a straightforward supporting result.

Disagreement on ICD regulation claims (C46-C53, C8, C90-C91). OpenEval finds the western blot and enzymatic activity data with statistical significance provide strong support, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to incomplete experimental documentation and missing loading controls.

Disagreement on domain mapping claims (C31-C33, C4, C34). OpenEval finds the systematic truncation analysis of 12 proteins provides consistent support for the 195-245 aa active domain, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to incomplete methodological transparency and missing loading controls.

Disagreement on novelty claims (C5-C6, C35, C65). OpenEval supports the phylogenetic analysis demonstrating this as a novel KDAC type, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, with one explicitly challenging the generalization to 'prokaryotes' as arbitrary without evidence from other species.

Disagreement on cofactor-independent deacetylase activity (C20-C28). OpenEval finds the dot blot, western blot, and systematic cofactor testing with appropriate controls provide strong support, while peer reviewers express uncertainty due to missing loading controls and incomplete methodological documentation.

Agreement on bioinformatics characterization (C16-C19, C22-C23). Both evaluations accept the homology analyses and control experiments with AhCobB and AhAcuC as establishing the distinct protein families and expected properties of known deacetylase types.

Partial agreement on substrate specificity (C66-C67, C76). OpenEval supports the validation experiments showing unique and shared substrate specificity, while peer reviewers accept the cooperation findings (C7, C39-C42) but raise methodological concerns about loading controls that create some uncertainty.

Disagreement on acetylome quantification (C36-C38). OpenEval finds the quantitative acetylome data with appropriate statistical analysis provides strong support, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, explicitly requesting complete loading controls and stating the data are insufficient to support the conclusions.

Agreement on substrate overlap and cooperation (C39-C42, C7). Both evaluations support the findings of shared substrates and functional cooperation among deacetylases, with peer reviewers explicitly accepting the cooperation claims despite raising methodological concerns about other aspects.

Agreement on inference of additional KDACs (C43-C44). Both evaluations accept this logical inference from the acetylome data showing ~90% of acetylation sites are not regulated by the three characterized deacetylases, treating it as a reasonable supporting conclusion.

Agreement on cooperation in acetylation homeostasis (C7, C77). Both evaluations support the inference about cooperation among KDACs based on overlapping substrates and co-regulation data, with peer reviewers explicitly accepting this finding.

OpenEval supports the quantitative acetylome comparisons to E. coli (C74-C75) based on data and appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific comparative claims.

OpenEval supports the acetylome findings (C80-C81) but notes caution about the priority claim (C82) lacking systematic review. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about first evidence.

OpenEval supports the database analysis and discussion of annotation conflicts (C68-C73) based on appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these nomenclature and annotation claims.
OpenEval supports the 3D structure prediction and mechanistic insights (C78-C79) based on structural analysis and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these structural claims.

OpenEval supports the ICD acetylation background and comparative analysis (C83-C89) based on established knowledge and new data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific ICD acetylation comparisons.
OpenEval supports the background knowledge claims (C1-C2, C54-C62) as appropriately cited context-setting information. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval supports the summary conclusion (C92) as appropriately synthesizing the collective experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this overall conclusion claim.
